title: Closed support commutes with derived limits of sequences
statement:
Use the standing setting of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible: a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with their condensed coefficient conventions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ its ring of integers. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All sites and products use the fixed size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, and let $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Pullbacks are the coefficient-compatible module pullbacks [def-sfb-module-upper-star], and $Rj_*$ is the total right derived module direct image [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $G(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, with the adjunction unit as its map, and $R\underline\Gamma_Z=RG$, as in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. For a finite locally free $\Lambda_S$-module $L$ (on a pro-étale covering, $L$ is isomorphic to $\Lambda_S^{\oplus r}$ with finite ranks $r\ge0$ allowed to vary), consider
$$
j^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(V,\Lambda),\quad u^*:D(Z,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda),\quad i^*:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(Z,\Lambda),\quad Rj_*:D(V,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda),
$$
$$
R\underline\Gamma_Z=i^*\fib(\mathrm{id}\to Rj_*j^*):D(X,\Lambda)\to D(Z,\Lambda),\quad u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda),\quad L[0]\otimes_{\Lambda_S}^{\mathrm L}-:D(S,\Lambda)\to D(S,\Lambda).
$$
Here $D(T,\Lambda)$ abbreviates the displayed pro-étale derived category; tensor is the derived tensor of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], equivalently ordinary termwise sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] for this $L$. Each listed functor $F$ is additive and triangulated, preserves all small products, and preserves fibers, meaning that it carries distinguished fiber triangles to distinguished fiber triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. It commutes with sequential derived limits in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]: for every tower $(K_n,t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n)_{n\ge0}$, applying $F$ to any Roos triangle
$$
H\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow H[1],\qquad P=\prod_nK_n,\qquad \mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1},
$$
and identifying $F(P)$ with $\prod_nF(K_n)$ by the canonical product comparison yields a Roos triangle for $(F(K_n),F(t_n))$. In particular $F(H)$ is a derived limit of the image tower. Every comparison to another such derived limit that completes these product identifications to a morphism of Roos triangles is an isomorphism; no canonical choice between arbitrary triangulated-category cones is asserted.

proof.text: The coefficient identification $f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies each module pullback here canonically with the lift of inverse image having the transported $\Lambda_X$-action, so no nontrivial scalar extension remains. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] separately to $i,j,u$ (a closed or open immersion is a locally closed immersion). Their sheaf functors are additive, exact and preserve all small limits, in particular products. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] the induced derived functors are termwise and triangulated. For every small family of representatives $(C_a)$, [det-pe-products-derived] computes the derived products on both source and target by termwise products; hence $f^*(\prod_a C_a)\cong\prod_a f^*C_a$ degree by degree, with the product projections. This proves the claims about $j^*,u^*,i^*$.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion (1), and the open slice restriction; derived.tex Tag 07KC, lemma-products

proof.text: The adjunction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] makes $j_*$ right adjoint to $j^*$ on module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], $j_*$ preserves small products. In particular $j_*j^*$ does so. Write $G(M)=i^*\ker(\eta_M:M\to j_*j^*M)$, as defined in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. Naturality of $\eta$ with respect to each product projection identifies $\eta_{\prod_aM_a}$ with the product of the $\eta_{M_a}$ under these product comparisons. Products and kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]: a tuple lies in this product kernel exactly when every coordinate lies in its kernel. Thus $\ker(\prod_a\eta_{M_a})\cong\prod_a\ker(\eta_{M_a})$. Applying product-preserving $i^*$ from step 1 shows $G(\prod_aM_a)\cong\prod_aG(M_a)$. The kernel construction is additive. For a finite diagram $(M_b)$, exactness of $j^*$ and finite-limit preservation of the right adjoint $j_*$ identify $j_*j^*(\lim_b M_b)$ with $\lim_b j_*j^*M_b$. Naturality against the limit projections identifies the unit map with $\lim_b\eta_{M_b}$. Sectionwise, an element of $\ker(\lim_b\eta_{M_b})$ is a compatible family whose every component is in $\ker\eta_{M_b}$, so this kernel is $\lim_b\ker\eta_{M_b}$. Exactness of $i^*$ now gives $G(\lim_bM_b)\cong\lim_bG(M_b)$, proving left exactness. This is the sheaf-level product-and-fiber calculation for the source's support construction.

proof.text:
Let $H$ be either of the additive sheaf functors $j_*$ and $G$ of step 2. Resolve an arbitrary small family of source complexes $(K_a)$ by K-injectives $(I_a)$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], on the fixed small site models. Sheaf products exist by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], the termwise product $I=\prod_a I_a$ is K-injective and represents $\prod_aK_a$ in the source derived category. Definition [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and step 2 therefore give
$$RH(\prod_aK_a)\cong H(\prod_aI_a)\cong\prod_aH(I_a).$$
By [det-pe-products-derived] on the target, the last complex represents $\prod_aRH(K_a)$. The isomorphism respects every projection, so it is the canonical derived product comparison. This proves all small product preservation for $Rj_*$ and $R\underline\Gamma_Z=RG$, including the empty product. This argument does not assume that $G$ sends an arbitrary complex to a derived model.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, lemma-product-K-injective; Tag 07KC, lemma-products; injectives.tex Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck

proof.text: Both source and target module categories have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to the additive functors $j_*$ and $G$. It makes $Rj_*$ and $RG$ triangulated. Together with step 1 this proves the same for $u^*RG$, and steps 1 and 3 give its product preservation: the comparison for a composite is the composite of the two product comparisons, as checked on each projection. The support functor in the statement is this $RG$: [sk-lem-formal-closed-support] (1) identifies it with $i^*\fib(\mathrm{id}\to Rj_*j^*)$. Thus the product calculation proves the source's closed-support claim for exactly its functor. A triangulated functor carries $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ to such a triangle, so when $A$ is a fiber of $B\to C$, its image is a fiber of the image map; this proves fiber preservation for all six functors already handled.

source.place: Open direct image and Closed support paragraphs; derived functor exactness

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda_S$ and $T_L=L\otimes_R-$. Its finite-limit preservation is [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-finite-free-tensor-exact], since the local finite-free covering here is precisely that node's hypothesis. It is additive and left adjoint to sheaf internal Hom by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], hence preserves finite colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Thus $T_L$ is exact and its termwise derived functor is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Explicitly, exactness preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology and their quotient, giving $H^q(T_LC)\cong T_LH^q(C)$. It therefore preserves acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms. By [def-pc-kflat-complex], $L[0]$ is K-flat: its tensor with any acyclic complex is the acyclic termwise complex $T_LC$, up to symmetry. Its terms are flat, since tensor by $L$ is exact and all other terms vanish. The equivalence $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] supplies, for every $C$, an object $P\in\mathcal P_R$ and an isomorphism $Q_RP\cong C$. Since $L[0]\in\mathcal P_R$, the same statement gives the canonical isomorphism $L[0]\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}Q_RP\cong Q_R(L\otimes_RP)=D(T_L)(Q_RP)$. This comparison is natural in $P$ and compatible with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms. Therefore it descends to $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R$ and along its equivalence with $D(R)$ to a natural isomorphism $L[0]\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}-\cong D(T_L)$. The statement's derived tensor of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules] is the two-variable left derived functor of the tensor of complexes, computed by replacing either argument by a K-flat resolution [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. Hence on $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$ it is also given by $Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$, naturally and compatibly with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms. The uniqueness-and-extension clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore identifies it naturally with the bifunctor used above. Thus the last functor in the statement, $L[0]\otimes_{\Lambda_S}^{\mathrm L}-$ in the sense of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], is the exact termwise functor $D(T_L)$; it too preserves distinguished fiber triangles.

proof.text:
For every small family $(M_a)$ of $R$-module sheaves the comparison $L\otimes_R\prod_aM_a\to\prod_a(L\otimes_RM_a)$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, restrict to an object $U$ of a single covering trivializing $L$. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], restriction is evaluation on the over-site, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] shows that it commutes with the displayed product. Tensor restricts to tensor: [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] gives $(L\otimes_RN)|_U\cong L|_U\otimes_{R_U}N|_U$ naturally in $N$, so the comparison restricts to the comparison for $L|_U$ and the family $(M_a|_U)$. Where $L|_U\cong R_U^{\oplus r}$, additivity of tensor and its unit isomorphism [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identify $R_U^{\oplus r}\otimes_{R_U}N$ with $N^{\oplus r}$ naturally in $N$, so the comparison is the coordinate reindexing isomorphism
$$(\prod_aM_a|_U)^{\oplus r}\cong\prod_a(M_a|_U)^{\oplus r}.$$
For finite $r$, the inverse groups together the $r$ coordinates for each $a$; this includes $r=0$ and the empty family. These inverses agree on overlaps because both invert the restriction of the same comparison; the sheaf axiom glues them to a global inverse. This local calculation requires neither a uniform rank nor a global free presentation.

proof.text: For any small family of complexes, use [det-pe-products-derived] on $S$ to represent its derived product by the termwise product. Step 5 identifies $L[0]\otimes_R^{\mathrm L}-$ with the exact termwise functor, and step 6 interchanges it with that product in each degree. The resulting comparison is induced by the same projections, so the tensor functor preserves all small derived products. With steps 1--4 this completes product and fiber preservation for every functor in the list.

source.place: Tensoring with L paragraph; passage from sheaf products to derived products

proof.text:
Let $F$ be any listed functor and $(K_n,t_n)$ any tower in its source. Products exist by [det-pe-products-derived] and a derived limit exists by [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (1). Write a chosen Roos triangle as in [def-weil-derived-limit], with $P=\prod_nK_n$ and $\mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Let $P'=\prod_nF(K_n)$, write $s'$ for its shift, and let $\phi:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ be the canonical product isomorphism already proved. For each $n$,
$$\mathrm{pr}'_n\phi F(s)=F(\mathrm{pr}_ns)=F(t_n)F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=F(t_n)\mathrm{pr}'_{n+1}\phi.$$
The product universal property gives $\phi F(s)=s'\phi$; additivity then gives $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$. Let $\chi_H:F(H[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H)[1]$ be the shift isomorphism of the triangulated functor, and write $\delta:P\to H[1]$ for the original connecting map. Applying $F$ to the Roos triangle and using $\phi$ on both product terms gives precisely a Roos triangle for the image tower, with first map $\phi\circ F(H\to P)$ and connecting map $\chi_H\circ F(\delta)\circ\phi^{-1}:P'\to F(H)[1]$. Thus $F(H)$ is a derived limit of the image tower. For another Roos triangle of that tower, rotate both triangles so that their first two terms are $P',P'$. Axiom TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes the identity on these terms to a morphism of triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], its third component is invertible. Rotating back proves that every comparison completing the product identifications is an isomorphism. The proof makes no uniqueness claim about that completion.

Local finite-free products and transition-map compatibility are proved explicitly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q144-05413a78b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item in full. That is all eight steps, the statements of all 26 cited nodes, the unit, the blueprint main-20261015 statement and proof, and the Stacks sources 09AA, 0BK6, 08TC, 03DH and 03EL. The delivery only changes the status to split; the reviewed proof already existed. The statement is correct and keeps every target clause. The correction from 'natural map' to 'Roos triangles go to Roos triangles, and every completing comparison is invertible' is justified by 08TC, which gives derived limits only up to non-unique isomorphism; it is not a weakening. Steps 1–5, 7 and 8 check out against their cited statements. Step 3's direct computation of products of K-injectives avoids the blueprint's 'products of distinguished triangles' claim, which is not automatic. Long step 5 (2224 characters) is one argument and stays: L[0] is K-flat with flat terms, and the two derived-tensor bifunctors are identified by the uniqueness clause of the descent node together with lem-sfb-derived-monoidal. No existing comparison node was found. FIX (C1/C4): step 6 was marked elementary but used that restriction to a localized site commutes with the sheaf tensor product. In the DAG, sheafification is defined only by its universal property, and existing nodes cover only topological-space or Zariski opens, not S_proét. I added the statement-only node lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction (Stacks 03EL applied to the localization morphism of 03DH; unsplit; created.item = this item; same unit). Step 6 now cites it and also cites lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed for R^r⊗N ≅ N^r; it is no longer marked elementary, and proof_deps is recomputed. I accept all 15 declared tool_uses. There is no duplicate, no cycle and no SGA citation, and the edge cases hold (Z=X, Z empty, S empty, L=0, zero tower).
